reason: The hypothesis combines the known effect of Mo addition on HfNbTaTiZr (P38, P40) with the edge-dislocation mechanism for high-temperature strength (P11, P13, P16, P17, P42, P47) into a specific prediction for a new composition (HfNbTaTi0.8Mo0.2Zr) and property changes (elastic modulus, thermal expansion), but the core idea of Mo substitution to enhance high-temperature strength via edge dislocation control is directly suggested by the existing literature, and the predicted outcome is a straightforward extrapolation.
copied_elements: Adding Mo to HfNbTaTiZr to study elemental effects (P38, P40)
Edge dislocation control of high-temperature strength (P11, P13, P16, P17, P42, P47)
Transition from screw to edge dislocation slip above a knee temperature (P13, P16)
Yield strength plateau at high temperatures (P5, P16)
